61: Streaming anomaly scoring must run on arriving events, while durable storage preserves data for later analysis.
The historical Kinesis SQL RCF function scores the stream, and Firehose delivers results to S3. The retired SQL service requires a different architecture for new deployments.
Self-managed Spark streaming and HDFS add substantial operations; HDFS replication is not a substitute for the requested durable S3 data lake.
Batch processing after writing to S3 does not score events as they arrive.
An on-demand Glue job followed by inference is a batch-oriented flow rather than the stated continuous scoring path.
62: Compressed events must be decoded before a streaming SQL engine can interpret their fields.
Historically, Lambda preprocessing could decompress incoming records for Kinesis SQL analytics, avoiding a store-then-query batch cycle. That SQL service is retired.
A general ETL job adds scheduling and processing latency instead of executing SQL continuously over arriving events.
A custom Kinesis consumer and Elasticsearch ingestion pipeline require more code than the historical managed preprocessing/SQL integration.
Firehose delivery to S3 includes buffering and still requires a separate query engine; it does not directly provide SQL over the live stream.
63: A small labeled tabular dataset with six categories calls for supervised multiclass classification.
XGBoost with multi:softmax predicts a class label among the six categories after appropriate encoding of the input features.
A deep CNN is designed around spatial or similarly structured input and is unnecessarily complex for this small tabular feature dataset.
A regression forest predicts numeric values; the number of trees does not define the output classes.
DeepAR forecasts related time series, not product categories from static labeled feature records.
64: Reducing redundant word forms can make a sparse vocabulary more statistically useful.
Syntax and entity detection add linguistic annotations but do not directly merge inflected variants or reduce the sparse vocabulary.
CBOW learns embeddings, but the proposed tool does not directly address normalization of the many rare surface word forms.
Stemming merges related forms, and suitable stopword removal reduces unnecessary vocabulary. Preserve negation and other sentiment-bearing words when choosing stopwords.
TF-IDF changes term weights but does not, by itself, merge variants or solve the low-frequency vocabulary problem.
65: Standardization puts numeric features on comparable scales using statistics fitted to the training data.
Quantile bins discard within-bin numeric detail and are not required merely to remove scale differences.
Feature cross-products create interactions and can amplify scale differences rather than remove them.
Subtract each feature's training mean and divide by its training standard deviation, producing zero-mean, unit-variance features when variance is nonzero.
Orthogonal sparse bigrams construct text features; they are unrelated to scaling continuous economic measurements.
66: Column pruning is especially valuable when queries read only a few columns from very wide records.
Parquet's columnar layout lets Athena read the requested 5–10 columns instead of scanning all 200 as row-oriented text.
JSON remains row-oriented and typically adds structural text, so it does not provide the same column-pruning benefit.
GZIP reduces CSV size but retains row-oriented parsing and can also limit file splitting for parallel reads.
XML adds a verbose row/document structure rather than efficient columnar access.
67: Orchestrate dependencies separately from distributed ETL execution and failure notification.
Step Functions can wait and coordinate the arrivals, Glue performs the large joins, and monitored failures can trigger CloudWatch/SNS notifications.
A notebook lifecycle script is not a robust distributed ETL orchestration platform for multi-terabyte joins and dependent jobs.
AWS Batch runs submitted compute jobs; this option does not supply the explicit dataset-arrival waiting and workflow coordination described in A.
Chaining Lambda functions is fragile for large joins and constrained by execution time and memory; Glue is designed for distributed ETL.
68: Dimensionality reduction can simplify many survey features before clustering respondents with similar patterns.
Factorization machines learn supervised feature interactions, but no prediction target or recommendation label is specified.
LDA primarily models topic mixtures in count-based document data, not arbitrary 500-feature survey records without further assumptions.
PCA can compress correlated, appropriately encoded survey features into fewer informative components.
k-means can group similarly represented respondents, helping identify population segments for planning.
Random Cut Forest detects unusual records rather than providing the main segmentation and dimensionality-reduction combination.
69: DeepAR learns shared temporal patterns across related product series rather than fitting each product entirely independently.
A standalone ARIMA model for a brand-new product lacks its own demand history and does not automatically transfer patterns from related products.

DeepAR can learn from related product histories and relevant features. Forecasting a new product still requires suitable context/covariates; it is not a guarantee of arbitrary zero-history forecasting.
k-means groups observations by similarity and does not directly produce a future demand time series.
A custom XGBoost forecasting pipeline needs engineered temporal features and training design; DeepAR provides the more direct cross-series forecasting approach.
70: Reading an SSE-KMS object requires both S3 object permission and permission to use the encryption key.
Permissive HTTP network rules do not grant S3 or KMS authorization and unnecessarily widen network access.
VPC access alone does not authorize object retrieval, and the relevant identity is the notebook execution role rather than an unspecified KMS role.
Give the notebook execution role S3 read permission and the required KMS decrypt authorization through the applicable IAM/key policies.
Selecting a key for the notebook's own storage encryption does not grant permission to decrypt objects already encrypted in S3.
71: Glue runs managed Spark ETL jobs and supports scheduled execution without a persistent customer-managed cluster.
A persistent EMR cluster can reuse Spark code but requires more cluster management and ongoing provisioned resources.
A scheduled Glue PySpark job reuses the transformation logic, joins the S3 inputs, and writes the consolidated output without managing servers.
Lambda is not a distributed Spark runtime for combining these large datasets and has execution-resource limits.
A streaming SQL rewrite changes both the batch schedule and the existing PySpark implementation, adding unnecessary migration work.
72: Feature selection can reduce overfitting while preserving the original features needed for coefficient interpretation.
L1 regularization can shrink some logistic-regression coefficients to zero, selecting a sparse set of interpretable predictors.
Adding features without evidence of missing signal increases complexity and can worsen the observed generalization gap.
Recursive feature elimination removes less useful original features and retains a subset whose model coefficients remain interpretable.
t-SNE creates nonlinear visualization coordinates, obscuring direct effects of the original features and not serving this interpretable classifier requirement.
Linear discriminant analysis projects features into combinations; those transformed axes do not preserve the requested direct original-feature effects as clearly.
73: Near-real-time defect detection requires continuous scoring, with a separate durable path for later analysis.
Notebook-based exploration is not a continuous low-latency detection pipeline, even if ingestion and storage are available.
Writing to S3 and then running an EMR analysis introduces a batch-style processing delay and additional cluster operations.
The proposed S3-first flow does not specify continuous endpoint invocation as events arrive.
Historically, Kinesis SQL RCF scored incoming metrics and Firehose archived them in S3. The retired SQL service makes this a historical exam answer.
74: A custom SageMaker algorithm uses a container registry for executable images and object storage for data/assets and artifacts.
Secrets Manager stores credentials; it is not the training container registry or the general dataset/artifact store.
CodeStar is not required to package and run a custom algorithm in SageMaker.
ECR stores the container image containing the custom algorithm and runtime dependencies.
SageMaker manages the training execution; an ECS cluster is not required to run that SageMaker training job.
S3 supplies training data and external assets and stores resulting artifacts. Algorithm hyperparameters are passed through the training-job configuration.
75: Convert sustainable requests per second to requests per minute, then apply the desired utilization safety factor.
10 is the safety-adjusted rate per second; the target metric in the question is measured per minute.
30 does not follow from the tested 20 RPS capacity and the 0.5 safety factor.
20 × 60 × 0.5 = 600 invocations per minute per instance, leaving the requested headroom.
2,400 effectively increases the target beyond tested capacity instead of halving it for safety.
76: Domain-specific pretrained embeddings transfer semantic information about specialized vocabulary into a sequence model.
TF-IDF is a document term-weighting representation, not the pretrained dense contextual word representation intended for the LSTM input.
Replacing LSTM cells with GRUs changes the architecture but does not add the missing domain knowledge after many architecture experiments.
A smaller learning rate changes optimization, but cannot supply semantic knowledge absent from the input representation.
Energy-domain word2vec vectors encode relationships among specialized terms, giving the existing LSTM a more informative initialization.
77: Streaming ingestion and scheduled workflow orchestration can feed existing EMR processing on different cadences.
DMS targets database migration and replication, not the general stream-plus-scheduled-EMR orchestration combination described.
Kinesis supplies a stream that compatible EMR consumers can read for near-real-time processing.
In the historical architecture, Data Pipeline schedules and coordinates data movement and EMR jobs for the periodic portion.
Athena queries data; it is not the ingestion or scheduling service feeding the existing MapReduce workflow.
Elasticsearch is a search/analytics destination, not the requested ingestion and batch-orchestration pair.
78: Hosting a locally trained model requires compatible inference code, a container image, and accessible serialized model artifacts.
Package compatible inference code and push the image to ECR; provide the separately serialized model artifacts in the location expected by SageMaker, commonly S3.
S3 stores model artifacts, but an inference container image is referenced from a supported container registry rather than uploaded as an S3 image object.
The standard SageMaker hosting workflow uses ECR for the inference image; this option substitutes Docker Hub and omits the intended registry setup.
Configuring Docker Hub is unnecessary when the image is being pushed to ECR and does not add a missing hosting requirement.
79: Object storage is a natural fit for a growing collection of raw images used by multiple analytics and ML services.
DynamoDB item-size limits and access patterns make it unsuitable for storing arbitrary image objects as the main dataset repository.
S3 scales the raw-image data lake independently of compute, and bucket/IAM policies restrict access to the designated principals.
An EMR HDFS cluster introduces capacity and lifecycle management; EC2 access control alone is not equivalent to object-level data-lake authorization.
EFS supplies a mounted file system and requires client/network setup; S3 offers broader direct integration for this raw-image data lake.
80: Dimensionality reduction compresses redundant input information into fewer features, reducing training work and potentially overfitting.
Self-correlation of a feature with itself is always one; this wording does not define a useful redundancy-removal method.
Rescaling features changes their magnitudes but leaves the number of highly correlated columns unchanged.
PCA or an autoencoder can represent the data in fewer dimensions while retaining substantial structure; choose the retained capacity through validation.
Sampling rows from clusters reduces observations rather than feature dimensionality and can discard useful examples without solving column redundancy.
